timing.basis: The 2026 SOP gives a service standard of about one week after approval of a rule change.

activities.name: Obtain a third-party inspection from a licensed professional

timing.basis: The County FAQ and 2026 SOP both say to expect about one week. Applicant reports range from same-day service when bundled with an electrician visit to approximately three weeks, but those reports are not representative samples.

activities.name: Prepare stamped structural letter

timing.basis: No County source states the preparation time.

activities.name: Submit the One-Day Solar Permit application

timing.basis: The 2026 SOP says submission occurs the same day or next business day after the set is complete. The earlier FAQ's advice to allow about a week includes pre-filing sheet corrections rather than merely transmitting a complete package.

activities.name: Pay the residential rooftop solar permit fee

timing.basis: The 2026 SOP requires payment the same day or next business day. Applicant reports of two to ten days for posting are inconsistent with the service standard and are treated as delayed cases.

activities.name: Screen the application at the counter

timing.basis: The 2026 SOP sets the service standard at the same day or next business day.

rework.reason: Missing documents or an unpaid fee cause the package to be returned to submission; staff record the missing item and do not advance a partial package.

activities.name: Review the submitted documents in the reviewer queue

timing.basis: The 2026 SOP sets a target of about one week per reviewer-queue pass. Complaint threads report materially longer aggregate queue times over repeated rounds, including approximately 74 to 81 days, and therefore describe the delayed upper tail rather than the median clean-file pass.

rework.reason: The County FAQ states that about four in ten applications require at least one correction round. The applicant corrects and resubmits documents on the existing case, which re-enters review without a second fee.

activities.name: Reconcile the deposit against the cost-recovery account

timing.basis: The 2026 SOP sets the service standard at the same day or next business day.

rework.reason: A receipt or deposit discrepancy is returned to the Solar Desk for correction of the case record before issuance.

activities.name: Issue the Instant Solar Permit and final inspection approval

timing.basis: County Code requires same-business-day issuance for a complete and compliant application; the 2026 SOP operationalizes this as same day or next business day.

activities.name: Add the case to the inspection route

timing.basis: The 2026 SOP requires routing the same day or next business day after issuance.

activities.name: Perform the single combined inspection

timing.basis: County Code schedules inspection for the next business day, and the 2026 SOP requires performance the same day or next business day after the case reaches the route. Complaint reports of five and 23 days are treated as delayed cases.

rework.reason: The 2026 SOP expressly sends violations requiring correction and resubmission back to application submission. The checklist prohibits concealing or energizing nonconforming work until resolution.

activities.name: Update the public permit register

timing.basis: The 2026 SOP requires the update the same day or next business day after the inspection result is recorded.

activities.name: Scan and archive the case file to records management

timing.basis: The 2026 SOP requires archiving the same day or next business day after the register update.

activities.name: Compile the annual report to the state agency

timing.basis: The 2026 SOP requires compilation within about one week after the reporting year closes.

activities.name: Issue denial letter

timing.basis: Two County applicant reports document written denials after multiple correction rounds, but no official County source states a denial service standard.

rework.reason: Applicant reports say denied applicants were told they could reapply or had to start over; no official source defines which existing artifacts may be reused.

edges.condition: Only if review flags a truss-framed roof with a clear span over 30 feet.
